es: Completa: « ___ I open the window? It’s very hot. »

why.en: “Can I open the window? It’s very hot.” “Can” + base verb says what you are able to do; the verb after it never changes. We use “Can I…?” to ask for permission.
why.fr: « Can I open the window? It’s very hot. » « Can » + verbe de base exprime ce que l’on sait ou peut faire ; le verbe qui suit ne change jamais. On utilise « Can I… ? » pour demander la permission.
why.es: « Can I open the window? It’s very hot. » « Can » + verbo base expresa lo que sabes o puedes hacer; el verbo que sigue no cambia. Se usa « Can I…? » para pedir permiso.

qa: Complete the sentence. blank I open the window? It's very hot.
aa: Can I open the window? It's very hot.

correct: Yes, I’ll have the fish, please.

why.en: In a restaurant, “I’ll have…” is a natural way to order.

qa: Someone says: Are you ready to order? What do you answer?
aa: Yes, I'll have the fish, please.

fr: Lis le texte, puis réponds.
es: Lee el texto y responde.

why.en: “The only problem is that it is always full at lunchtime.”
why.fr: « The only problem is that it is always full at lunchtime » (toujours plein à midi).
why.es: « The only problem is that it is always full at lunchtime » (siempre está lleno a mediodía).

qa: The new café in our street is great. It opens at seven, and the coffee is cheap. The only problem is that it is always full at lunchtime. What is the problem with the café?

q: Complete: “This soup is ___ hot. I can’t eat it.”
fr: Complète : « This soup is ___ hot. I can’t eat it. »
es: Completa: « This soup is ___ hot. I can’t eat it. »

why.en: “This soup is too hot. I can’t eat it.” “Too” = more than you want (a problem); “enough” = as much as you need.
why.fr: « This soup is too hot. I can’t eat it. » « Too » = trop (c’est un problème) ; « enough » = assez, autant qu’il faut.
why.es: « This soup is too hot. I can’t eat it. » « Too » = demasiado (es un problema); « enough » = suficiente.

qa: Complete the sentence. This soup is blank hot. I can't eat it.
aa: This soup is too hot. I can't eat it.

q: Complete: “___ brothers and sisters do you have?”
fr: Complète : « ___ brothers and sisters do you have? »
es: Completa: « ___ brothers and sisters do you have? »

why.en: “How many brothers and sisters do you have?” “How much” asks about price or quantity of something uncountable; “How many” asks about a number of things.
why.fr: « How many brothers and sisters do you have? » « How much » demande un prix ou une quantité d’indénombrable ; « How many » demande un nombre d’objets.
why.es: « How many brothers and sisters do you have? » « How much » pregunta un precio o una cantidad incontable; « How many » pregunta cuántas cosas.

qa: Complete the sentence. blank brothers and sisters do you have?
aa: How many brothers and sisters do you have?

q: Complete: “This present is ___ you. Happy birthday!”
fr: Complète : « This present is ___ you. Happy birthday! »
es: Completa: « This present is ___ you. Happy birthday! »

why.en: “This present is for you. Happy birthday!” “For” shows who receives something.
why.fr: « This present is for you. Happy birthday! » « For » indique le destinataire.
why.es: « This present is for you. Happy birthday! » « For » indica quién lo recibe.

qa: Complete the sentence. This present is blank you. Happy birthday!
aa: This present is for you. Happy birthday!

q: Complete: “He is very good ___ tennis.”
fr: Complète : « He is very good ___ tennis. »
es: Completa: « He is very good ___ tennis. »

why.en: “He is very good at tennis.” We say “good at” something.
why.fr: « He is very good at tennis. » On dit « good at » quelque chose.
why.es: « He is very good at tennis. » Se dice « good at » algo.

qa: Complete the sentence. He is very good blank tennis.
aa: He is very good at tennis.

q: Someone says: “How was your trip?” What do you answer?
fr: Quelqu’un te dit : « How was your trip? » Que réponds-tu ?
es: Alguien te dice: « How was your trip? » ¿Qué respondes?

why.en: Talking about a finished trip: “It was great.”
why.fr: Pour parler d’un voyage terminé : « It was great. »
why.es: Para hablar de un viaje terminado: « It was great. »

qa: Someone says: How was your trip? What do you answer?

q: What does “I’m fed up” mean?
fr: Que veut dire « I’m fed up » ?
es: ¿Qué significa « I’m fed up »?
correct: I’m tired of it and annoyed.

why.en: “Fed up” = bored or annoyed by something that lasts too long.
why.fr: « Fed up » = en avoir assez, être lassé.
why.es: « Fed up » = estar harto/a.

qa: What does I'm fed up mean?
aa: I'm tired of it and annoyed.

q: Complete: “We ___ go to the cinema on Fridays.”
fr: Complète : « We ___ go to the cinema on Fridays. »
es: Completa: « We ___ go to the cinema on Fridays. »

why.en: “We usually go to the cinema on Fridays.” Adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) go before the main verb but after “be”.
why.fr: « We usually go to the cinema on Fridays. » Les adverbes de fréquence (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) se placent avant le verbe, mais après « be ».
why.es: « We usually go to the cinema on Fridays. » Los adverbios de frecuencia (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) van antes del verbo, pero después de « be ».

qa: Complete the sentence. We blank go to the cinema on Fridays.
aa: We usually go to the cinema on Fridays.

q: Complete: “I ___ TV when you called me.”
fr: Complète : « I ___ TV when you called me. »
es: Completa: « I ___ TV when you called me. »

why.en: “I was watching TV when you called me.” The past continuous (was / were + verb-ing) shows what was in progress at a moment in the past.
why.fr: « I was watching TV when you called me. » Le past continuous (was / were + verbe en -ing) montre ce qui était en cours à un moment du passé.
why.es: « I was watching TV when you called me. » El past continuous (was / were + verbo en -ing) muestra lo que estaba en curso en un momento del pasado.

qa: Complete the sentence. I blank TV when you called me.
aa: I was watching TV when you called me.

es: ¿Qué frase es correcta?

why.en: “Do you like + verb-ing?” is the normal form.
why.fr: « Do you like + verbe en -ing ? » est la forme normale.
why.es: « Do you like + verbo en -ing? » es la forma normal.
